title: Leaf-print vase
summary: In Chulucanas, in northern Peru, potters shape slim-necked vases and decorate them by resist: leaves and a protective coating keep parts of the clay pale while the firing in sawdust darkens the rest. Each leaf is printed in negative. Here you shape a vase and choose the colour of each band.
howToPlay: Look at the lit vase on its mat: it shows the shape and the colour of each band.
Drag across the turning clay to set how wide each row is.
Press Glaze, then tap a band and a colour: smoke black, cream resist or burnt sienna.
Press Check to see your stars, or Watch and learn to see a round played for you.
rules: Shape counts for 70 percent of the score: the closer each of the 12 rows is to the width of the lit target, the better.
Finish counts for 30 percent: a band scores when it carries the same swatch as the target.
The leaf prints are part of the picture; the colour of the band decides what the leaf shows against.
Undo takes back one stroke; Reshape goes back to the clay; Reset starts the shape again.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40.
heritageNote: Chulucanas is a town in the dry forest of the Piura region in northern Peru. Its potters shape and polish the ware, apply a resist with leaves, and fire it in kilns with sawdust, so the covered parts stay pale and the rest turns dark.
